page: Amazon Web Services r6g.12xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the 64-bit ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 Graviton processor architecture. The instance provides 48 dedicated physical cores clocked at 2.5 GHz without simultaneous multithreading, running one thread per core. Memory capacity totals 384.0 GB of RAM, establishing an 8.0 GB memory-to-core allocation. The CPU subsystem includes 64 KB of L1 data cache and 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core alongside a shared 32 MB L3 cache, backed by hardware-accelerated AES cryptography.

The server does not include local instance storage, requiring remote Elastic Block Store volumes for persistent disk operations. Network connectivity provides a baseline throughput of 20 Gbps, and the configuration includes zero graphics processing units. In synthetic evaluation, the 48-core ARM setup delivers strong multi-core performance, achieving a stress-ng multi-core score of 72,807.75. Memory bandwidth demonstrates solid throughput, sustaining 163.3 GB/sec on large read blocks and 77.62 GB/sec on large write operations.

Benchmark outcomes indicate specific architectural tradeoffs. Single-threaded metrics are comparatively lower, with Geekbench single-core scoring 952.0 and single-threaded gzip compression recording 20.31 GB/sec. Similarly, large language model inference throughput remains low across testing tiers. Conversely, parallel execution remains competitive, evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core rating of 12,954.0 and 54.73 million Redis SET operations per second.

From an efficiency standpoint, the dedicated Graviton cores deliver consistent compute allocation combined with dense memory capacity. Amazon Web Services r6g.12xlarge is suited for in-memory databases like Redis or Memcached, distributed caching tiers, data analytics engines, and memory-intensive microservice architectures where broad multi-core scaling takes precedence over single-threaded burst capability.
description: Amazon Web Services r6g.12xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 48 dedicated ARM64 Neoverse-N1 cores operating at 2.5 GHz, paired with 384.0 GB of system RAM at an 8.0 GB per core ratio. Powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the instance delivers 20 Gbps baseline networking and hardware AES acceleration. It contains no bundled local storage or GPUs, relying on networked storage architectures. Benchmark data highlights strong multi-core processing with a stress-ng score of 72,807.75 and robust caching throughput at 54.73 million Redis SET operations per second, counterbalanced by modest single-threaded performance. Delivering dense memory scaling and consistent core dedication without hyperthreading contention, r6g.12xlarge is well tailored for enterprise in-memory databases, distributed caching layers, and high-concurrency multi-threaded data processing workloads.
